newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Won's fall puts lid on S.Korean gold demand.
newsitem.headline: Won's fall puts lid on S.Korean gold demand.

text.p: South Korean domestic gold prices have fallen in the past week on tumbling international prices, but the fall has not boosted demand due to a corresponding sharp decline in the won, bullion dealers said on Tuesday.
"We had expected some good buying interest by people from March, the start of the wedding season, but the won dampened the mood," one dealer said.

Gold producer LG Metals' daily selling price for the precious metal, which is regarded as a benchmark for the local bullion wholesale market, fell on Tuesday to 10,280 won per gram from 10,470 won a week ago.
The company's silver price was unchanged from the previous week at 163 won a gram
According to the data from the Unification Ministry, South Korea imported 4,738 kgs of gold from North Korea in 1996, compared with 6,409 kgs a year earlier.
South Korea also imported 26,955 kgs of silver from North Korea in 1996, down from 34,267 kgsin the previous year.

The fall in imports of precious metals from North Korea reflected the hightened tensions between the two countries since a top North Korean ideologue sought politial asylum at the South Korean mission in Beijing and a defector from the
Traders said most South Korean firms preferred to import North Korean precious metals because they attract a three percent import tax exemption.
The telegraphic transfer selling rate for customers, posted by the Korea Exchange Bank, fell to 878.00 won against the dollar from 867.00 won a week ago.
The rate is regarded as a benchmark for local foreign exchange rates for companies.

On Monday, the Association of Foreign Trading Agents of Korea (AFTAK) said South Korea's gold import price was slightly down to $11.33 per gram in February from $11.57 in January, while the silver price rose to $168.94 per kg from $155.99.
